summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 100 views. The best videos (Clap Switch, PIR Sensor, Gyro Robot, Line Follower, IR Robot) explain a familiar gadget or robot with a surprising or 'it can't do X' hook, and they earn the most likes, saves and shares. Everyday-object videos (taps, lifts, smoke alarms, remote) get far fewer views and almost no saves or shares, and the English Arduino video has no Instagram presence at all.
winningPattern: Robot or sensor-behavior subjects that makers relate to (clap switch, PIR, line follower, gyro, IR obstacle robot), with a contrarian or curiosity hook ('doesn't listen to claps, only noise', 'doesn't see you', 'has no brain', 'would fall instantly'). Titles are short Hinglish with one bold claim, an emoji and #shorts. Instagram Reels is the main driver, with saves and shares highest on the build-it-yourself style topics.
doMore: Lead with a surprising 'X doesn't actually do Y' claim in the first line, as the Clap Switch and PIR videos do
Pick robot and Arduino-module topics (motors, servo, line/obstacle robots, balancing) over generic household devices
Make each video useful to save: end with the one component or wiring tip people can note down
Add a share trigger such as a common myth or 'send this to a friend building a robot'
Post on Instagram first and test a different, more search-friendly title and hook on YouTube, since it lags badly there
stopDoing: Making near-duplicate topics (two IR sensor, two tap, two smoke detector videos) that split the audience and underperform
Generic 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai? 🤔' titles on everyday objects with no surprising angle
Publishing English or any video on one platform only
